Veil of the Spire

The Yolubilis River begins high on the slopes of Mount Spire, just below the tree line, as a trickle that turns into a series of waterfalls. These waterfalls gather multiple streams as they surge downward, and the tallest, called the Veil of the Spire, falls more than 300 feet into a large pool that is the river's highest navigable point. Behind the waterfalls is an extensive networks of caves, some of which contain their own streams and falls. Many of these caves are riddled with cave fishers, chardas, and other monsters. 266087461:
Black Ink Lake

Black Ink Lake is a frigid yet roiling lake of iron gall ink located on the side of Arazlant Mox on the Isle of Kortos at an elevation of 13,000 feet. It is believed to be the final resting place of Norgorber's mortal effects before his ascension to godhood.⁠

Legends suggest the lake's distinctive composition comes from disposed documents describing Norgorber's crimes. The Court of Black Paper operates a shrine on its shores that uses the lake's ink in occult documents, and for submerging new advocates in occasionally fatal initiations.⁠

Norgorberites make pilgrimages to the site to sacrifice secrets of their own into its depths. Divers who attempt to retrieve items from it find it not only impossibly cold, deep, and dark to navigate, but also sense forces that seem bent on taking hold of them.⁠

Parts of stone ruins submerged within the lake are visible on its surface, and a small stone island is positioned at its center.⁠
274091611:
Imperial Prison

The Imperial Prison is a massive structure near the western bank of the Nosam River.⁠ The facility houses most of Molthune's criminals, but in accordance with the nation's ideology, it is dedicated to the rehabilitation of prisoners so they can reintegrate into society and contribute to it. The guards are well-trained and assisted by teachers and clergy who offer their services in rehabilitation programs. The prison is divided into two areas: one for those who have committed minor crimes or who have not caused permanent harm, and the high-security zone, which contains the nation's most dangerous criminals.⁠

The more progressive version of the prison works well, allowing inmates to receive education and skills training, and most become model citizens upon release. Warden Lonnox Rydel runs the prison, though he has neglected many of his duties, falsifying funds and selling prisoners to the hryngar for profit.⁠
275026211:
Jerikal's Ales

Jerikal's Ales is a cantina and brewery located in the Docks of Katapesh city and is uniquely run by a cleric of Shelyn called Jerikal Ashworth who has picked brewing as his chosen medium. The interior is dedicated to Shelyn: filled with beautiful statuary, fresh flowers and other beautifications that his patrons can enjoy along with his unique brews. Despite being run by a worshipper of Shelyn, it is like many traditional breweries, a site of worship for followers of Cayden Cailean, the Drunken Hero; this mini congregation is led by Tomlin Orlof who gets along well with Jerikal. Jerikal's Ales is renowned for it unique "priest in a bottle" brews which are combination of magical potions and alcoholic beverages.⁠ Jerikal is also a source of endless rumours especially adventure related ones, in his adventuring days he even acquired a map leading to a catacomb beneath Pale Mountain filled with treasure.⁠
286630241:
Mbaiki

In the past, the folk of the city of Mbaiki revered the animals of the jungle, and the jaguar above all others. The people all wished to emulate the jaguar—and something answered their call. The people rejoiced until it became clear that instead of being shapechangers they were condemned to live in jaguar form forever. In their rage they destroyed their city and then they moved into the jungle in small groups. It is said that some of the jungle's jaguars retain the knowledge of the Mbakai tribe, and can offer sage advice to those who know how to ask.⁠

Today, the remains of the city are home to the most numerous tribe of halflings in the Kaava Lands, the Hazh'a. They revere Lamashtu and Zura, and collect the heads of intruders.⁠

Statue Street

Statue Street is a long stretch of road in the Absalom district of Westgate.⁠

Appropriately named, the street contains dozens of scattered statues in various poses. These are the remnants of an Absalom tradition that has only recently been outlawed. In order to prevent prison overcrowding, nonviolent offenders were sometimes allowed to compete for a pardon in a race to outrun an enraged gorgon. The fortunate or skilful who evade the beast are granted a pardon for their crimes, while others now decorate the area with contorted expressions of shock, defiance, or terror.

Although ultimately considered unethical at best, there are many in the community who are upset that this tradition has been made illegal.⁠

Last Rites

Last Rites is a store in the Ankar-Te Ring district of the Varisian city of Kaer Maga. It is owned and run by Horus Ilaktya, who also oversees this unusual neighborhood with High Priestess Shamalay Kasan. Horus is a talented necromancer, and Last Rites is a supplier of custom-created undead for use as menial servants, mounts, and laborers. He prefers to refer to his merchandise as "Twice-Born", rather than undead, and thinks there is nothing wrong with his chosen profession. Since his creations are usually homicidal after being imbued with unlife, Horus has created special control-amulets known as death's head talisman, which allow the purchaser full control over his "reborn" minions.

Horus is always looking for fresh "raw materials" for his work, and will readily purchase fresh corpses. However, he is careful not to be seen to encourage grave-robbing, so he always checks the provenance of the bodies he buys.⁠

In 4719 AR, a gnome pathfinder found the location, raided it, and reported it as a Thassilonian ruin in the Pathfinder Chronicles.⁠ When the shoanti clans learned of this, they called an emergency meeting to decide whether to expel the Pathfinder Society from their lands altogether, becoming their enemies. Sardis Township

Sardis Township is a large town on the upper reaches of the River Porthmos in eastern Taldor's Porthmos Gap.⁠

The prefectural capital of the Porthmos Prefecture, Sardis extends for well over a mile in every direction as it was formed as a dozen small mining communities that grew together around rich veins of lead and other minerals. The settlement sits on the chaotic, polluted landscape that stretches just a few miles inland from the South River. Technically, the piers, refineries, and warehouses are also part of the township's domain. Despite being depressing and miserable, Sardis generates a great deal of wealth, trading high-quality metals for foodstuffs to supplement their own meagre crops.⁠

Although not known as a trade hub, Sardis does profit from trade caravans and travelling merchants. Centaur tribes from the Whistling Plains sometimes make the trek this far into Taldor for trade and some even choose to remain. Many are enlisted as enforcers by the local Grand Duke.⁠

Sardis Township is home to both the infamous Porthmos Prison and the governor of the Porthmos Prefecture, Grand Duke Thestro Briarsmith. The former is populated with the enemies of the latter.⁠

Trackless Storm

The Trackless Storm is an endless stretch of sandstorm in southern Katapesh near the border with Nex. The trackless storm rages year-round regardless of the surrounding weather conditions, although the severity of the storm varies. Sometimes the Trackless Storm is little more than a mild dust cloud, while other times it blows strong enough to scour flesh from bone. The landscape within the storm constantly changes as the winds alter the sand dunes.

Numerous rumours and legends are connected with the Trackless Storm. Some claim that a field of hardy, untouched pesh lies at the heart of the storm,⁠ while others claim that the Stone Sorcerer's legendary Sanctum of Sand resides within a valley hidden inside its swirling winds.⁠

Heavywater Perch

Heavywater Perch is a tiny site, little more than a single large rock near the southern end of Pangalley Atoll in the Shackles. The site's sole resident is a beautiful merfolk, Crimson Clepsana, with a tail of an enormous red snapper. She can usually be found sitting atop the rock when the Screaming Reaver is leaving or returning to port. The residents of Fort Benbem stay away from Heavywater Perch for fear of being enchanted by Clepsana's captivating song that lures many unwary sailors to their deaths. Captain Coal-Dark has informed her crew that anyone found staring at the sensuous merfolk while aboard her ship will receive a dozen lashes from her wicked cat-o'-nine-tails. As a precaution, she uses moist kelp to plug her crew's ears. Some of the crew wonder why Coal-Dark fails to simply take care of the seductress herself.⁠
633671521:
Spiralcross Cemetery


The Spiralcross Cemetery is the largest and most prestigious cemetery in all of Absalom, where Primarch]s, nobles, and high priests are buried. Located next to the Ahnkamen Estate, this cemetery is a labyrinth of vaults and shrines belonging to families with over four millennia of history. A large church of Pharasma stands among the tombs, and its presence, along with the proximity to Mother Jackal, means that few undead awaken in the area.⁠

There are several ghost stories about the place, but only one seems true: white orbs are seen moving through the cemetery at night, and it is said that they may be codes used by spies in the city, although no one has confirmed their purpose.⁠

Cicatrix

The Cicatrix is a blasted wasteland on the southwestern edge of the Tanglebriar in the elven nation of Kyonin. Crowded with camouflaged oozes, it is avoided by both elves and the nearby demons.⁠
634417591:
Thunderhold

The fortress of Thunderhold on the isle of Flintyreach in the Lands of the Linnorm Kings, is ruled by the charismatic hill giant chieftain Gorgnak who leads a semi-loyal band of hill giant, ettin, and troll warriors.⁠ The giants who live in the mountains of the island's interior are the greatest threat to the dromaar community of Averaka. The Averaka giant slayers have dedicated themselves to the eradication of their monstrous neighbors.⁠
637250261:
Sallowshore

Sallowshore is a port town on the coast of Geb directly east from Thornhearth. The town appears to be sinking into the ocean, with half the buildings already partially sunken under the water. The upper floors that poke above the water are connected by shoddy wooden bridges.⁠

651523411:
Thistleguard Station

The Thistleguard Station is the base from which the Ivy District guard operates. Located north of the Ivy District Park, it has a holding cell for up to 10 criminals to be detained until they are prosecuted. The Thistleguard does not concern itself with minor crimes, as it wishes to maintain a smooth relationship with the neighborhoods, and instead only goes after violent acts that disrupt the residents. One exception to this system is that performers who are not members of the Street Performers and Actors' Guild are more frequently arrested by the guard, and it doesn't take a genius to connect the conflicting interests with Nomarch Alain Always. They come into conflict with the Brotherhood of Abadar, which wants the law to be followed to the fullest extent, and nobles and merchants hire them to protect their merchandise since the guard does not investigate incidents of theft.⁠
655917471:
Citadel of the Weary Sky

The Citadel of the Weary Sky, formerly known as the Jaizun Citadel, is a mysterious and enigmatic historical site located in the realm of Rahadoum. It holds a significant place in the history of the Jistka Imperium, a once-powerful empire known for its mastery of elemental magic and extraplanar conjurations.⁠⁠
666559111:
Sundown Street

Sundown Street is a curving street near the city wall in the Ivy District, a few blocks from the bustling Flower Street Market. This street is renowned for housing the three most prestigious and sought-after tailors in all of Absalom: Ambroz Black, Al Amir Kai, and Madame Theodora Signe. It takes more than just money to gain the attention of these busy tailors; one also has to invite them to dinners, performances, and galas to secure a commission. The other cosmetics shops on the street benefit indirectly from the "big three"'s reputation, and only the elite of the elite frequent this area regularly.⁠
675479661:
Woodsedge

The home of one of the fathers of the revolution, Darl Jubannich (who wrote the damning book On Government that helped start the Red Revolution), Woodsedge has always served as the traditional home for dissident thought and radical philosophies in Galt. Even with the country in its current state, nothing has changed. No matter who is currently in power, one can almost guarantee that the opposition to them will begin in Woodsedge, and any visitor is almost certain to find some sort of dissident movement afoot.⁠

The Slace Block

687036581:
Lilywhite

Lilywhite is a small pirate town on the western coast of Motaku Isle in the Shackles that is home to a large number of worshipers of Cayden Cailean. It is the smallest of Motaku's settlements and was founded in 4682 AR by two pirates, Delemona Burie and Shaggard Halleck, devotees of Cayden Cailean. Alongside the foundation of the town, the pair funded the construction of a grand stone temple to the Drunken Hero. Halleck was killed in an alcohol-fueled duel in 4692 AR. Halleck's son, Little Shaggard, and Burie are the town's pirate lords.⁠
704344311:
Evergreen Park

Evergreen Park, located in the Eastgate district, is the city's largest park, maintaining a perpetual spring thanks to the efforts of the Children of Spring, a Gozreh cult led by Lady Evigail of House Wycomb. At the center of the park is an open-air altar, often visited by sailors before embarking on voyages to distant lands.⁠
710301971:
Deadeye Lodge

The wooden Deadeye Lodge is the city of Magnimar's church of Erastil, and is located in the northeast of the Keystone district on the edge of Seerspring Garden.

Looking more like a rustic hunting cabin, Deadeye Lodge seems quite out of place among the townhouses of the city, but that does not seem to bother the devotees of Old Deadeye, who attend in large numbers. Its head priest, Father Lorgell Fendus, holds services three times-a-week, and is known for his welcoming nature. The Lodge also hosts a dozen archers who serve their god by keeping the streets of Keystone safe for all. This brings them into occasional conflict with the similarly armed followers of Calistria's Dome of the Savored Sting, whose methods and morals while maintaining the peace are quite different.⁠
713169361:
Laekastel

The Chelaxian city of Laekastel is located on northern shores of the Inner Sea, where the Brastle River flows into the Bay of Deng.⁠⁠⁠
715329601:
Fort Faelon

Fort Faelon is an abandoned Nirmathi fort. Located along the coast north from Tamran, this fort overlooks the waters of Lake Encarthan from the marshy area where it was built.⁠
717366671:
Devildrome

The Devildrome is a semi-legal summoning arena where two mages pit their summoned beings against either other summoned beings or gladiators. Betting is the primary source of income, and locals enjoy the violence commonplace here.⁠
722510221:
Copperwood

Copperwood is a small town located northeast of Absalom just outside the city's walls that is the home of many of Absalom's laborers, tradesmen, and domestic servants.⁠ Originally a tent city of unskilled laborers who could not afford to live in the city proper, conditions steadily improved over the centuries until Copperwood became a town in its own right. The locals are often known as "Copperheads".⁠
725966951:
Crested Falcon

The Crested Falcon is a restaurant in the Heights District of Korvosa.⁠⁠
729141891:
Snemmevik

Snemmevik is the northernmost town in Almhult, located at the head of a bay in the Gulf of Svallmundr. It serves as a handy base for prospectors seeking gold in the nearby Hellrung Mountains.⁠ The Maganis River empties into the gulf nearby.⁠⁠
737639141:
Chapel of Guilts

The Ustalavic county of Barstoi boasts three Pharasmin monasteries: the Chapel of Guilts; the Mother of Skulls; and the Vault of Tears. The Chapel of Guilts is located in the north-west of the county near the source of the Delgavia River and is by far the most well known and feared.⁠
766190281:
Constabulary

The Constabulary is an elegant office that serves as the base for the Widdershins guard. Commander Taius Jessen is in charge of protecting the streets, and in the basement, a jail holds the district's criminals—a concept alien to the rest of the city, which exacts its own "justice" by taking revenge on those who wrong them.⁠
793470191:
Earthnavel

In the eastern Tusk Mountains of the Realm of the Mammoth Lords lies a deep pit that resembles an inverted 13-layer ziggurat. The layers are littered with the bones of massive animals; and the lower the layer, the larger the bones, until they dwarf those of the largest creatures known to walk the surface of Golarion today.⁠

At the bottom of this pit is an opening just large enough to admit an average-sized humanoid, known as the Earthnavel, or sipapu to the local Kellid tribes. Below it stretch miles of freezing-cold tunnels which lead down into Nar-Voth, the upper layer of the Darklands. These passages show signs of collapse, suggesting that there may have once been larger tunnels here that extended beneath Nar-Voth into the deeper Darklands. It is possible many large beasts of the Tolguth in the Realm of the Mammoth Lords migrated there from Deep Tolguth in Orv via now-collapsed tunnels.⁠
813975431:
Bazaar of Sails

The Bazaar of Sails is the largest free market in Varisia. Located in Dockway, in the Shore region of Magnimar, the Bazaar of Sails is adjacent to the waterfront, wedged between the Seacleft and the Varisian Gulf, and nearly under the Shadow of the Irespan.

The Bazaar of Sails is probably the busiest district of the city, filled with the hustle and bustle of traders from dozens of nations all competing for space, attention, and profit. From Osirian spices to Andoren wood to Chelaxian clothing, the markets are filled with goods of every sort. With such a variety of wealth on display one might imagine the district to be riddled with crime, but it is well policed, though not by the Magnimar city watch.

Sabriyya Kalmeralm bears the title "Princess of the Market", which she inherited from her missing father Nazir Kalmeralm; with the title comes the responsibility for keeping the markets reasonably safe through whatever means necessary. Some critics view Sabriyya as little more than Magnimar's most open crime boss, but those who trade in the Bazaar of Sails understand the service she provides even if it sometime requires unsavoury methods.⁠
817636221:
Danjing

Danjing is a vast metropolis in the eastern reaches of the Successor State of Lingshen and its inhabitants number almost 100,000 people.⁠ It is located near a unique, massive, impenetrable, unnaturally perfect pillar of resonant, humming crystal that predates the known history of Tian Xia. The crystal's mysteries have drawn large numbers of nagaji, magic users, and alchemists to the site, making the city one of Lingshen's most diverse.⁠
823795341:
Canary House

The Canary House is a rather exclusive inn in Kaer Maga, owned by Alaeh A'kaan, who wields considerable influence in the area. The establishment only admits the wealthiest of guests, and those whose attire displeases Alaeh are turned away.⁠ Expensive bird meat is the main delicacy here, and several murals of Garundi birds adorn the walls. Hanging from the ceiling are cages with golden bars where "Songbirds", slave girls who sing and dance, hop from cage to cage for the enjoyment of the guests below.⁠
825934531:
Citadel Rivad

The oldest of the citadels of the Hellknights, Citadel Rivad squats in the Turanian Hills northwest of Westcrown, the Twilight City and former capital of Cheliax. It is a solemn jail to heretical scrolls, quartos, and banned lore, and is zealously guarded by the Order of the Rack.⁠
833690111:
Tirchin

Tirchin is the capital of the nation of Mishyria located on the southern Kardaji Bay coast of the country.⁠
835643011:
Haldun

Haldun is a town on the southern edge of the nation of Rahadoum, situated on the main pass linking Rahadoum with the southern lands. At one time it was a thriving centre of trade, dealing with Lirgen and the other lands to the south. The advent of the Eye of Abendego destroyed Lirgen, turning the area into a hurricane-blasted wilderness.⁠

As of 4711 AR, however, Haldun had become a fortress town guarding Rahadoum against incursions of monsters and cultists, and is the centre of the defensive network known as the Rainwall. Its inhabitants are hardy folk who take a perverse pride in their harsh lives, and see the devastation to the south as a warning as to what happens to those who trust their lives to deities.⁠
858782711:
Eodred's Walk

Eodred's Walk is a collection of stores in the Varisian city of Korvosa situated near Eodred's Square and is comprised of fourteen shops forming a semicircle. There's an established collaboration between the vendors in Eodred's Walk and the merchants in the Gold Market where the stalls focus more on food products and minor crafts, while the shops in the Gold Market offer specialized services and various permanent goods.⁠

City Hall

877560521:
Jeggare's Jug

Jeggare's Jug, known by Korvosan locals as Jeggy's Jug, is the first tavern built in the Old Dock neighborhood of Old Korvosa.⁠⁠ The tavern draws a working-class crowd and maintains a sometimes violent rivalry with the rougher Sticky Mermaid tavern.⁠
877632621:
Tomb of Statues

The Tomb of Statues is the burial place of Pharaoh An-Hepsu III's family and servants, located on the western banks of Osirion's River Sphinx north of the city of An. Unlike in similar tombs, where the family and retainers of a pharaoh were buried alive or put to death following the monarch's passing, An-Hepsu III took advantage of his medusa consort's power, and had them all turned to stone.⁠⁠
885326081:
Zulran's Equines

Zulran's Equines is a sprawling horse ranch belonging to An'Aldane Zulran, guildmaster of the Imperial Union of Breeders. His horses and camels are regarded as some of the finest in all of Katapesh, if not the entire Inner Sea. The horsemaster's animals are bred for one thing: speed, and for this reason they are greatly valued by collectors. Zulran's reputation for breeding fast horses is matched only by his reputation for being a legendary haggler, marking his horses up to well above the usual rate.

The ranch is also a profitable riding school. An'Aldane's riding school is shockingly expensive but well worth the price, as those who complete his school ride away with unique and enviable skills.

A recent theft of one of his finest chargers by a kholo bandit named Bristlemane has left An'Aldrane infuriated and offering a 1,000-gold-piece reward for anyone than can return the horse and the head of the offender.⁠
885822201:
Mut

Mut is a small city located on the peninsula at the southern side of the mouth of the Porthmos River on Taldor's Inner Sea coast, about 40 miles downriver from the capital city of Oppara.⁠

The city is famous for its grand lighthouse, known as Glory's Flame.⁠
890123101:
Rolgrimmdur

Rolgrimmdur is built among the ruins of Grakodan by Khadon's engineers and is one of the most fortified dwarven cities in Five Kings Mountains.⁠ It is located about 50 miles southwest of the capital city of Highhelm.⁠
899611331:
Dragon Temple

The Dragon Temple, also known as the Celestial Dragon Temple, is a retreat in the Wall of Heaven mountains on the western border of Quain that is a famous center for martial arts training in Tian Xia. It is also a temple dedicated to the god Irori. Students come from across the continent, including distant Minkai, to study under the masters of the Dragon Temple.⁠
912635891:
Frog pond

One of the two foul-smelling hot springs at the source of the Skunk River also serves as a frog pond for two aggressive giant frogs. They fiercely defend their 150-foot-wide pond and its immediate surroundings, but are quick to retreat into the swampy, bubbling water when their life is threatened. For those who can tolerate the pungent smell of rotten eggs it releases, the warm waters of the pond are quite pleasant.⁠
922002751:
Rat-Taker's Palace

The Rat-Taker's Palace is the base of operations for the city's cleaners, responsible for maintaining the sewers, repairing pipes, and pest control. The building was abandoned after the earthquake, but they quickly returned to reclaim it, as its ostentatious appearance was too tempting to not move back in. Unfortunately, during their absence, a rat infestation took hold and continues to be a problem to this day.⁠

Prophet's Home

928451691:
Maggot Tree

The Maggot Tree is in the center of the Hagwood, a huge, twisted tree that was once home to a coven of hags, of which only the Mother of Flies has survived. In 4710 AR, agents of the Council of Thieves attacked the tree, attempting to burn it down to destroy the hag who knew the only weakness in their new leader's plan.⁠
951007991:
High Harbor

High Harbor is a once-grand settlement reduced to ruins⁠ located on the northeast coast of the Scrape region of the Isle of Kortos.⁠
956270351:
Pyre Crest

Pyre Crest is a volcano in the area of Brazen Peaks that remains uninhabited by the kholo that otherwise litter the range. Not even scrubs grow on the scorched sides of Pyre Crest though the eruption that covered the sides of the mountain in lava occurred centuries ago. Blackened tracks of hardened magma cover the surface of the mountain like veins.⁠
979731021:
Udayasankar

Udayasankar is a small village in the northern reaches of the Golden Basin region of the Impossible Kingdoms of Vudra. A nearby cave contains the Stone Egg of Jayalakshmi, an incredibly powerful artifact that opened the minds of monks who first found it during the ancient Age of Destiny.⁠
980460581:
Thornhearth

Thornhearth is a small thorp in Geb just south of the Axanir River.⁠
984920331:
Harse

Founded in 4536 AR by Sarwin Harse, the town of Harse is an important gateway between Korvosa's inland holdings and its seaward settlements. Positioned at the junction of the Sarwin and Falcon Rivers, the town's twin ferries provide the easiest means of crossing both rivers for travelers in the area.⁠

The town is built on a narrow strip of land between the Sarwin and Falcon rivers, and has been a river crossing since the time before the Chelaxian arrived. It contains only a few dozen buildings, including a church of Erastil run by Mother Tasa Seganni, two grocers, and two taverns (the Spotted Pony, and the Nag Bag). Most of the inhabitants do not live in the village proper, but on isolated farms and ranches spread about the local countryside.⁠ The town is known for its horse and livestock breeding, and holds a large rodeo at the Harse Market each year to determine Varisia's top riders and animals.⁠⁠
995594231:
Broken Monastery

The Broken Monastery was the base of operations for the Brothers of the Seal before their split into two factions which fought over the building, even setting it on fire twice, and locals avoid the place as an omen.⁠
1001598581:
Mezdrubal

Mezdrubal is a small town at the southwestern region of Devil's Arches island in the Shackles. It is ruled by a petty buccaneer called Longbeard who resents his tribute that Hell Harbor demands at the beginning of each month.

Longbeard could not even think to refuse to pay his tribute, and he usually takes out his frustration at the poor victims of his cruel and often arbitrary judgement. Mezdrubal's ruler is also known for his love of fine clothing and jewelry, and many pirate vessels head to his town to sell such wares to Longbeard.⁠
1002359091:
Dammartorp

Dammartorp is a small settlement on the Marbleflow River in Irrisen's Hoarwood province. It is jointly ruled by the Jadwigas Tereza and Tsviata, twin sisters locked in a struggle for control of the town.⁠

The peasantry are divided between the two baronesses and they even frequent different markets and taverns and spit on the ground when passing one another. The peasant followers of Lady Tereza are led by Viglund Lyubienko, who is also the owner of the Tavern on the Water, while those who favor Lady Tsviata are led by the prominent wool seller Zora Oblatov.⁠

Bandits infest the trade route between Dammartorp and Hoarwood but the baronesses are too engaged in their quarrel to address the problem.⁠
1003795841:
Liachora

Liachora was the capital of the Iblydan archipelago city-state of Pol-Liachora that also included the city of Aelyosos. It was destroyed by the thalassic behemoth Ousmariku at the beginning of the Age of Lost Omens, in a battle during which many Iblydan hero-gods were killed.⁠⁠⁠ Its citizens were either killed in the attack or fled to Aelyosos, which became the city-state's inheritor-capital. The ruins of Liachora have since been claimed by sedacthies.⁠
1005155921:
Avenue of the Hopeful

The Avenue of the Hopeful is a winding street in Absalom's Ascendant Court and a busy market catering to those fascinated by the Test of the Starstone: hopefuls, followers, worshippers, and the merchants, pickpockets, and charlatans who hope to make money from them.⁠ Some of the sincere hopefuls have lived on the street for years, while others are merely confidence men.⁠ Merchants offer religious symbols, holy water, and relics, as well as "faith papers", which indicate the popularity of a hopeful deity.⁠ The booth of the Masked God of Secrets, a presumed hopeful, is a front for an organization that collects and sells secrets.⁠
1014155481:
Okim

Okim is one of the many cities of the Tian Xia nation of Linvarre, which was formerly the Taldan colony of Amanandar. Formerly a military outpost, Okim is now primarily known for its fireworks production, which is said to have drawn organized criminals from Seidoyaji and Todorokaze seeking to sell black powder across neighboring Kwanlai.⁠
1025723501:
Vladmirr

Vladmirr is an isolated Iobarian town on the shores of the Castrovin Sea. The southernmost major settlement in Iobaria, Vladmirr is surrounded by the delta of the Pharrus River, close to the Icerime Peaks. Though the town is rich in natural resources with a bounty of arable lands and precious minerals, its lack of a protected port and the Castrovin's high waves often leaves the town overlooked in favour of Kridorn or Mirnbay.⁠
1027666761:
Zunderwal Hold

Zunderwal Hold is a long-fallen dwarven fortress in the Stained Peaks near Avistan's approach to the Crown of the World. It has long been occupied by bugbears, who fight an ongoing battle for supremacy over who should hold the title of "Huntmaster of the Hold".⁠⁠

Valdemar Villa

Kaleb Valdemar, son of the late Ethram Valdemar and head of House Valdemar, runs Valdemar Villa in Magnimar when not visiting Sandpoint.⁠⁠
1045129921:
Whitegate Market

Whitegate Market is located close to the centre of the aristocratic district known as The Greens in Kintargo. It is the city's most affluent market, and the streets surrounding it are filled with wealthy smiths of platinum, gold, and silver.⁠
1050290941:
Tekeh

Tekeh is a city in the Ketz Desert of Qadira.⁠
1056522101:
Clicking Caverns

The Clicking Caverns are set of underground tunnels and caverns known to connect to the Darklands of the continent of Tian Xia and are located on the border between the nations of Xa Hoi and Nagajor. They are inhabited by flesh-eating clockwork constructs haunted by the souls of their extinct builders.⁠⁠⁠
1057318091:
Cader Boneyard

The Cader Boneyard was abandoned over a hundred years ago. Located in the northernmost part of the Rego Cader, Westcrown, vegetation is now reclaiming the crypts and tombs that fill the place. Those buried here do not rest well, and sightings of the undead keep people away.⁠
1067014661:
Whitewillow

The Whitewillow was a swamp in the Shimmerglens of shallow water with beautiful trees and lovely flowers cared for by Myriana, but when she was killed and tormented with the death and resurrection as an undead of her lover, the trees turned black and its waters became fetid and twisted.⁠
1069893261:
Urchin's Maw

Located in the Arcadian Ocean west of Acisazi and northwest of the Dismal Nitch, the entrance to the underwater cave known as Urchin's Maw gapes from the side of the continental shelf, overlooking a precipitous drop into the inky depths below. It earns its name from the riot of sizable deep sea urchins that dwell on the rock face surrounding the cave entrance.⁠
1071320631:
Crosspine

Located along the southeastern edge of the Uskwood, Crosspine is a village that stands out due to its distinctive practice of guiding a remarkably elevated proportion of its youth into the paths of arcane and druidic learning. Among its notable denizens are Isiem, a prominent shadowcaller, and Ascaros, a renowned sorcerer skilled in shadow magic.⁠

Kalit

Versade Villa

Versade Villa is the headquarters of House Versade, one of the aristocratic families of the Varisian city of Magnimar best known for throwing amazing parties. It is located at the end of a long line of upper-class villas in the Alabaster District, directly beside Valdemar Villa.⁠⁠

Gatefoot

Gatefoot sits as the western end of the Pillar Wall in the Korvosan district of the Heights. The massive foot is one of the remnants of ancient Thassilon that still dot Korvosa and was clearly part of some ancient wall. Many scholars think it most likely also serves as part of some sort of enormous gate.⁠
1090761351:
Waldsby

Waldsby is a typical peasant village located near the Hoarwood Forest in the Irriseni province of Hoarwood.⁠
1094416361:
Dawnflower Library

The Dawnflower Library is a temple of Sarenrae and library located on 10 Dawnflower Street in the town of Otari, on the southern coast of the Isle of Kortos. Its high priestess is Vandy Banderdash, a talkative halfling woman. While the temple also hosts shrines to Cayden Cailean, Erastil, and Gozreh, most of the building is dedicated to its publicly available collection of books. The temple also offers medicine, magical healing, and divine spellcasting services.⁠
1100882111:
Ehur

Ehur is a city in Qadira. Lying in the center of the Ketz Desert, this genie city is where denizens of the various Elemental Planes have their embassies and serves as a trading hub for these people within Qadira.⁠
1112451561:
Thom

Thom is a small gnomish town in the central River Kingdoms.⁠
1117468261:
Haigui Wan

Haigui Wan is a small town in Shenchu Bay island in the Shackles. It is built on the northeastern peninsula of the island to serve as the base of Shenchu's defensive fleet which protects the island from Dahak's Fang. Most of the fleet's ten ships are kobuksons ("turtle ships").⁠
1119643051:
Thousand Relics Pass

Thousand Relics Pass is a mountain pass through the northern World's Edge Mountains of Taldor. It is bordered to the west by the Falling River and to the east by Aroden's Eye.⁠
1122519651:
Citadel of Flame

The Citadel of Flame was the headquarters of a cult of the archdevil Moloch that arose in the Meraz Desert of Qadira three centuries ago. It is located in the western Meraz Desert, near the shores of Obari Ocean.⁠⁠

Thought to have been annihilated and covered by a stand storm, the citadel was rediscovered by the Pathfinder Society in 4709 AR. Upon sending Pathfinders to investigate, it was discovered that the cult was resurgent and under the control of a powerful cleric of Moloch named Hafshi Al-Moloch, who hoped to open a permanent planar portal to Malebolge. The Pathfinders defeated the cult and returned its magical idol of Moloch to the Grand Lodge in Absalom.⁠
1134052401:
Embrey's Armory

Embrey's Armory is no ordinary shop, as here the legendary blacksmith Engleton Embrey forges weapons and armor of such quality that one might have to travel to other planes to find better. The shop's exterior is unremarkable, a simple stone block near the local park, but inside, three forges are constantly at work, and the clang of metal against metal assaults the ears. When a soldier speaks of Absalom's metal, they are referring to the metal produced here, and the name Engleton inspires fear in the enemies who oppose his creations and courage in the allies of those who wear them. He has a white beard and a wrinkled face, always displaying humility, even though he knows he is among the best in the world and he channels that pride into his creations, not into cheap arrogance. Knowing he won't live forever, he trains a trio of apprentices to uphold his legacy, who can be seen working in the armory.⁠
1152102321:
Saarbotten

As of 4713 AR, Saarbotten was a border town on the Thundering River in the Irriseni province known as the Verge.⁠

Saarboten is organized entirely toward the support of the raiding parties that cross the border south and west into the Lands of the Linnorm Kings. The town hosts permanent armories, camps and warehouses. The Wintercrux town of Dalun has the responsibility to supply Saarbotten's food while Morozny and Vasterborg provide weapons and armor. Baroness Urgalaena is the bloodthirsty, enthusiastic ruler of the town, mocking publicly her sister Baroness Nadya of Dalun for her diplomatic efforts in order to improve trade with the Ulfen people. Baroness Urgalaena hosts the vicious "Crimson Tournaments" every week.⁠

Saarbotten was opposite the lands of Southmoor and Ysborg to the south and the eastern part of the Grungir Forest to the west. The nearest Ulfen settlements are the village of Whiterook in Southmoor and Losthome in the Grungir Forest. Saarbotten is also close to the gnome village of Delmon's Glen in the forest.⁠

As of 4719 AR, the region around Saarbotten was within the borders of the Lands of the Linnorm Kings.⁠
1153605981:
The Slace Block

The Slace Block was located in the Lower City and guarded by two squads of the Zephyr Guard. While vendors displayed slaves to potential buyers on the stone platform, intelligent creatures of all kinds were sold. Some, like ogres or trolls, could not be purchased carelessly, as they could tear their owners apart. However, there was always someone arrogant enough to end up as pieces of meat shortly after buying them. The Steel Falcons operated by assassinating and sabotaging slavers, and the Pactmasters offered bounties on their heads for a time. In 4722 AR Katapesh outlawed slavery, and this market ceased operations.⁠
1166521191:
Bone Garden

The Bone Garden is an unusual kholo cemetery located in the foothills of the Brazen Peaks along Osirion's southern border with Katapesh. Firstly, it is unusual, because most kholo do not bury their dead, preferring to leave them to be picked apart by hyenas and vultures. Secondly, the Bone Garden is unusual because those who are interred here do not stay in the ground for long. This is because the graveyard is tended by kholo priestesses of Urgathoa, who are happy to accept the bodies of any fallen kholo brought here by its tribe-mates and convert them to skeletons and zombies. The devotees of the Pallid Princess have amassed a sizable army of the undead, which they trade with the Pharaoh of Fangs to augment his troops.⁠⁠
1177789861:
Bluestone

Bluestone is a hamlet on the border of Molthune and Nirmathas that frequently changes hands between the two nations. It was originally built around a circle of stones and a shrine to Gozreh. Its frequent changes in ownership has weakened the town's economy considerably, and the village no longer contains many elaborate structures outside the original Gozren shrine.⁠
1180287641:
Cerulean Docks

The Cerulean Docks are small docks where ships disembark in Kerse, though their size is normal given that they are decorated with marble pillars and precious stones throughout. Rhivash is the dock chief, and it is his efforts that keep the hundreds of ships moving through the area each day in perfect motion.⁠
1183988841:
Great Palace

The Great Palace—located in the eastern first tier of Urgir in the Hold of Belkzen, just inside the city's eastern gate—is the location of the vacant Throne of Urgir. The last overlord to sit upon the throne was Grask Uldeth,⁠ who was assassinated in 4716 AR; as of 4720 AR, his remains still sat upon the throne with a sword plunged through his chest. His effective successor Ardax the White-Hair, a former advisor to Uldeth, served as acting overlord after the assassination and refuses to fill the throne, instead claiming the title of steward and ruling from the Halls of the Closed Fist.⁠

The exterior of the building bears massive letters in the Dwarven language that spell "Urgir",⁠ an Orc word meaning "first home". These letters were carved in -3708 AR by the city's conquering orc forces, led by Belkzen, after defeating its dwarven defenders in the Battle of Nine Stones; before the orcs, the city was the Sky Citadel of Koldukar.⁠ The palace is surrounded by the historic Plaza of Sky.⁠
1189871731:
Kuruban Swamp

Kuruban Swamp is a line of heavily wooded islands in Vudra's Open Bridge region that was not fully connected to the mainland when the Obari Ocean receded in 4606 AR. Instead, the upheaval created a semi-sunken mangrove swamp. Unlike the rest of Open Bridge, which is infested with hordes of horrific aberrations, Kuruban Swamp is controlled by sedacthies who ruthlessly protect its borders. The sedacthies seem to be searching amongst the ancient ruins that dot the swamp, but no one knows for what.⁠
1190401541:
Promise

Promise, the capital and only settlement of any significance on the island nation of Hermea in the Steaming Sea, is located in the island's southern corner.⁠
1194384901:
Tents of Erukh

The Tents of Erukh is an encampment of impossibly beautiful people located within the Alavah Peninsula of Qadira. The camp is built around a massive tent owned by the exiled jaathoom wizard Erukh, for whom the camp is named. Erukh refuses to explain why he was banished from the Elemental Plane of Air to the Universe. He accepts no gifts from those looking to curry his favour and instead asks the supplicant to perform a task for him. The few who manage to achieve their assigned tasks are invited deeper into the Tents of Erukh, where supposedly even more wonders abound.⁠
1201618331:
Vaneo Drovenge

Vaneo Drovenge was the three-story mansion of the powerful House Drovenge, which wielded considerable influence in the city. But in 4710 AR, the family collapsed, and thieves stole all the mansion's valuables.⁠
1204289511:
Drydock

The drydock of Iron Harbor is a massive building used for the construction, maintenance, and repair of ships, boats, and other watercraft that enter the village.⁠ It is overseen by Birger Frodeson, a no-nonsense human who will nevertheless allow visitors to use the drydock as a place to sleep if they get on his good side or pay him a gold piece per night.⁠
1220447201:
Tree of the Thousand Eyes

The Tree of the Thousand Eyes is a colossal tree located in the south of the Jolizpan Forest in Xopatl.⁠ The tree is named for the many patterns covering it that closely resemble the eyes of a peacock's tail.

Those who live nearby believe that the Tree of the Thousand Eyes grew from the heart of the chicome coatl that died when a fragment of the Aeon Star struck it. This legendary event occurred thousands of years ago during the formation of the Jolizpan Forest. According to local legend, the heart of the chicome coatl still exists at the centre of the Tree of the Thousand Eyes and, if someone could make this heart beat again, it would resurrect the powerful coatl.⁠
1226710901:
Justnoque

Justnoque is a sunken city underneath the Steaming Sea, off the coast of Varisia and the Lands of the Linnorm Kings. In the times of ancient Thassilon, Justnoque was a center of learning and metallurgy in the kingdom of Cyrusian, but it now lies ruined under the waves; only about a dozen slick black stones jutting from the water mark its presence. The sunken city is feared by the Linnorm Kings, but adventurers sometimes set sail from the Linnorm King city of Jol to explore Justnoque; the few that return tell tales of aquatic giants inhabiting the ruins.⁠⁠
1238797771:
Irrere

The exclusively gnomish town of Irrere, located on the island of Irrere in the Ironbound Archipelago, is renowned for its exotic architecture. The establishment of the gnome monastery of Shay Citadels close to the town led to an increase in the town's population.⁠⁠

Its residents enforce a policy of extreme isolationism, although gnomes frequently make pilgrimages to Irrere, especially those who are feeling the effects of the Bleaching. The monks of the Shay Citadels research this ancestral curse and seek ways to resist its effects.⁠⁠ The town is also welcoming to duskwalker gnomes.⁠

Although few natives leave Irrere, those who do often possess great wisdom and insight—a result of deep self-reflection typically uncharacteristic of other gnomes.⁠
1242009051:
Phaendar

The town of Phaendar is located in southern Nirmathas on the southern bank of the Marideth River near the Chernasardo region of the Fangwood. Despite its small size, it is one of the largest settlements in the Nesmian Plains. The town grew out of a Chelaxian stronghold which itself was built on top of an outpost of the Shining Crusade. The residents of Phaendar, most of whom are skilled craftspeople, mistrust authority and the town has little to no standing government. Most of the town's law enforcement needs are provided by the Chernasardo Rangers who frequent the town to trade for supplies.⁠

Ridonport

Ridonport is a small coastal city located in the empire of Taldor, south of the city of Cassomir. The settlement is best known as the home of General Arnisant, the Taldan hero responsible for imprisoning Tar-Baphon, the Whispering Tyrant.⁠

Crowtop

Crowtop is an abandoned village in the Irriseni province of Hoarwood. Inexplicably, the village has not decayed or been buried by the snow. It stands just as it did over a thousand years ago. Nobody knows its original name, but it is now called Crowtop because of the thousands of crows that perch on the village's roofs and fence posts in strange silence.⁠ It is one of the few places in Irrisen where crows can be found in large numbers, as they are normally killed on sight.⁠

People say the village's residents suddenly vanished. Within the houses, meals sit unfinished and chores half-completed, but nobody is known to have actually set foot in the place. It is said that Crowtop is cursed and the crows are the souls of all the Ulfen slain in Baba Yaga's conquest. They also say the crows serve some nefarious purpose for the White Witches,⁠ while others claim that they are psychopomps.⁠

Thrune's Chance

Thrune's Chance is a coastal hamlet on the edge of the North Plains in the west of Nidal on that nation's border with Cheliax.⁠ The hamlet is managed by the Chelaxian embassy in Pangolais. Most of its inhabitants are ambassadors or agents of House Thrune, under the command of Admiral Ferixia Rone. Each year, the embassy selects five Nidalese to work for a year at Thrune's Chance on joint activities between the two nations. If they complete the year successfully, the chosen ones can become Chelaxian citizens and live in the empire.⁠

Thrune's Chance is an opportunity for the Umbral Court to rid itself of citizens dissatisfied with the government without provoking them to openly rebel. Those who take this opportunity are never allowed to return to Nidal.⁠

1379283151:
Monastery of the Veil

The Monastery of the Veil is home to an isolated and mysterious group of monks. It is located in the remote Hungry Mountains in the eastern reaches of Ulcazar county in Ustalav.⁠⁠
1380249011:
Deadeye's Haunt

Deadeye's Haunt is a narrow valley on the border between Molthune and Nirmathas, at the southern edge of Fangwood. It is the site of the bloodiest battle in the war between the two nations.⁠
1384171171:
Westerhold

Westerhold is the richest of Absalom's outlying towns. Members of Absalom's wealthiest families own small estates in Westerhold. The town is also known for its large number of dwarven inhabitants and trustworthy stables.⁠
1407483011:
Apertan

Apertan is a city in the Arcadian nation of Xopatl located to the south of the country's centre. Apertan is home to the largest market in all Xopatl that attracts merchants and traders from across the land. The market itself is an enormous open-air tower with many levels, each teaming with shops and stalls. Visitors use a system of platforms to raise and lower themselves between the various stalls and shops.⁠
1413442081:
Ruba's Shop

Ruba's Shop is a scrivener's shop in the Old Kintargo district of Kintargo that also serves as a notary and translator. Unbeknownst to most, the owner—the elderly Varisian, Ruba Fenquay—is also an accomplished forger whose other illegal sideline business is copying forbidden texts.⁠
1426258291:
Wheel Unbroken

The Wheel Unbroken, a multistory workshop of wizardry and magical research located in the Tarheel Promenade district of Kaer Maga, Varisia, also serves as the guildhall for the Arcanists' Circle. This cooperative approach has established the Circle as a place to buy or commission advanced and manufactured magic items.⁠

The castle is presumably named after Count Andachi of Tamrivena who led a successful defense of Ustalav in the 41st century AR, before being betrayed by his head general, Kazavon. Castle Andachi is avoided by all, as it is known to be the lair of powerful creatures or haunts.⁠⁠⁠
1460723481:
Goblin King's Court

The Goblin King's Court is a series of wooden walkways and towers resembling a castle amidst the flooded houses of The Puddles. It is where Zusgut resides, acting as king. The goblins' short stature makes them reluctant to walk through the wet streets, so they hop from house to house to reach the court. Zusgut has advisors from all over Golarion who come to the city following tales of his fame.⁠ The goblins have devised a system that repairs and removes planks depending on the tide, and they have prepared a large stage where they perform daily. Therefore, it is easy to find the court simply by listening for the tremendous noise they make shouting during theatrical performances.⁠
1468759741:

Infinite Ossuary

The Infinite Ossuary is a ruined fortress in the Nesmian Plains of what is now Nirmathas controlled by undead, constructs, and elementals. The original fortress was built on top of an onyx mine, with the strategic purpose to secure the spell components to animate the armies of Tar-Baphon.

As of 4717 AR, the Infinite Ossuary still held hundreds of preserved corpses ready to be raised as undead reinforcements, as well as dormant undead and the sleeping General Kros Catternine, a graveknight.⁠
1482882451:
Samsara Oasis

Samsara Oasis is a small town established by calikangs horrified at their role in the destruction of the region. They use Samsara Oasis as a place to meet and research restoration efforts to try to make up for this.⁠
1484930251:
Brimstone Springs

Brimstone Springs is a small settlement high in the Mindspin Mountains of Nidal known for its hot springs: the Soulsheen Baths. Hundreds of people from all over the region come every year to soak in its sulfur-rich mineral waters that fall in natural cascades, giving the town a rather unpleasant smell. These waters then collect to form the source of the Sulfur River, which flows westward out of the mountains toward Usk Lake. Brimstone Springs has also gained a certain amount of notoriety from the golden dream, a special, day-long immersion in poisonous waters that, if it doesn't kill the user, gives him or her visions of the afterlife while permanently dying the skin a deep yellow.⁠

Gold Manticore Fount

The Gold Manticore Fount is located in one of the poorest neighborhoods of Pangolais. The fountain has a reputation for granting wishes to people with pure hearts who are in immediate need. It is said that the fountain has helped homeless people, children, and lonely souls in their greatest times of need. The truth is that the fountain itself is not magical; the one granting wishes is Astarathian, a gold dragon with a human identity, who considers the problems he hears and either hires help for those in need or assists them himself.⁠
1521624791:
Tempest

Tempest is a nightclub in the Ivy District that was formerly a theater with a second floor containing apartments. Thanks to the illusions employed by the establishment, an esoteric and incomprehensible aesthetic is revealed, even though the common man is not permitted entry if they were the establishment would make no sense to them. Models pose in strange clothing, and niche artists use the stage for plays whose symbolism is convolutedly difficult to understand. The second floor is reserved for the elite, serving as the apartment of a painter whose disturbing murals cover the walls and who hated both affection and wealth. The sealed balcony is the residence of Zozzler Vondorun, the High Priest of Zon-Kuthon in Absalom, and with a touch of his hand, he can reveal the secret temple hidden behind the grotesque paintings.⁠
1527520711:
Pit of Zedoran

The Pit of Zedoran is a vast sinkhole within the depths of the Northern Fangwood. Streams of water carrying leaves and organic debris cascade down its sides, and layers of moss and lichen cover hanging vines and ancient roots. The thick forest canopy allows little sunlight to reach the moss-covered earth.

The pit is named for the green dragon Zedoran who as of 4722 AR still laired here.⁠ At the edge of the central pit is a wooden cage lift, manually operated by Zedoran's minions. There are two cages, one at the top and the other at the bottom of the pit, each large enough to hold eight humans.⁠
1530521991:
Icegraves

The Icegraves is the traditional burial site for the leaders of the Varki people in the Linnorm Kingdom of Icemark. After having their brains and entrails removed (which are offered to the sky on a platform), the Varki bury the bodies in a grave melted out of the ice. Anyone who visits the burial site can see countless bodies amidst their burial goods perfectly preserved in the ice.⁠
1531502881:
House of Golden Veils

The House of Golden Veils is the largest bank in Kintargo and a temple to the god Abadar. It is located in the northeastern corner of the city's Temple Hill district. As of 4724 AR its high priest was Mhelrem Gesteliel.⁠
1540012731:
Schloss Caromarc

Schloss Caromarc is an abandoned castle in the northeast of the Ustalavic county of Vieland, and is the former residence of Vieland's ex-ruler, Count Alpon Caromarc.⁠⁠
1551769211:
Chateau Douleurs

Chateau Douleurs is home to the Caliphvaso family and is located in the north of the Ustalavic county of Caliphas.⁠

Located on the eastern shore of Lake Raiteso, Chateau Douleurs boasts a paradise of labyrinthine gardens, statue-guarded pavilions, strange menageries, and luxurious retreats. The palace also contains the accumulated art, treasures, and decadences of the Caliphvaso clan. Yet few ever look upon the estate grounds or are permitted into the palace's interior, as a legion of deadly family guards defend the grounds with lethal efficiency. Such extreme measures to ensure privacy has spawned countless rumors of orgies, murderous hunts and various sordid family secrets.⁠

The halls of the chateau are haunted by the ghost of Ralagen Caliphvaso.⁠
1590150581:
Blackhill's

Blackhill's is a tavern in Eastgate that at first glance looks like a thatched roof a foot off the ground, leading to a constantly ventilated cellar where Dege Blackhill creates his famous spicy drinks, popular with those from Numeria. 1640809921:
Lightning Stones

According to ancient Garundi legend, the Lightning Stones mark a battleground between earth and air elementals. The stones glow when struck by lightning, revealing runes and glyphs otherwise invisible to observers. 1719624431:
Firewatch Peaks

The Firewatch Peaks are a series of squat bunkers manned by soldiers from Ustalav located in the Tusk Mountains of the Hold of Belkzen, just south of Whisperfall Pass.⁠

In total, there are twelve bunkers in operation, all under the control of the County of Canterwall and with the intention of monitoring orc (and sometimes dragon) activity in the area. The structures themselves predate the inhabitants of Ustalav, however, instead bearing markings of dwarven design.

In addition to underground tunnels, connecting each fortress, individual bunkers can communicate to each other (and the outside world) via trained hawks. More impressive is that in times of attack the stone roofs are capable of being lowered into the ground, making the bunkers virtually impervious to attack. This makes the defenses ideal against the ever-present threat of dragon attacks from Raschka-Tor.⁠

The fortifications are often tested by orc attack, most notably from the nearby Skull Eater tribe.⁠
1727741551:
Ardis

Ardis is the former capital of the Immortal Principality of Ustalav. It is located in the eastern region of Soivoda, in the County of Ardeal and is the largest settlement in Ardeal. The city contains many decaying estates and fallow fields.
1730359391:
Ashen Bulwark

The Ashen Bulwark is an abandoned dwarven fortress.⁠
1750238521:
Desgard's Thousand Columns

Desgard's Thousand Columns is an ancient Thassilonian ruin in eastern Varisia. It is a field featuring a large number of towered pillars and pylons of jagged crystal. They were used by the runelords of Sloth, particularly Krune, for conjuring armies of extraplanar forces to defend the realm of Haruka.⁠ They were activated by secret runes given to Krune by Lissala.⁠
1765949311:
Velashu Ferry

Located half way between the Cyphergate and Maskyr's Island, the Velashu Ferry is run by Grimas Oltedler.⁠
1770350371:
Prophet's Academy

Prophet's Academy is a vast manor house in the north-east of the Coins district of Absalom, purchased by Trevlin Crest and Ilrava Drogand, two followers of the Prophecies of Kalistrade who came to Absalom from Kerse to acquire the city's great riches. They obtain their wealth not through trade but through education, as it serves as an academy where their discipline is taught and connections are forged among the wealthy students who attend.⁠
1790636501:
Shimmerford

Shimmerford is a town in the River Kingdoms known for legends of the cryptid Mosquito Witch, in whose name the town stages an annual festival.⁠
1790987231:
Torcova

Torcova is a small town in northwestern Taldor in the southwestern foothills of the Fog Peaks in Northern Tandak Prefecture.⁠⁠ Outside of the town, lies the manor home of a local noble, Lord Sauton Beane, who hides a terrible secret. He is secretly an ogrekin, albeit a handsome one, who has gone through seven wives in the hopes of begetting a human offspring. He has not succeeded so far, and has locked his monstrous progeny in a cave beneath his home after murdering their mothers. He only releases his ogrekin children to punish his enemies or kidnap his next wife.⁠
1792004161:
Pillars of Dream

The Pillars of Dream is a strange monument associated with dreams, capable of putting anyone who touches them to sleep. The pillars float thirty feet in the air and are made of an unrecognizable, strange metal. Those who look through the center between the two pillars see a night sky that doesn't appear to be that of Golarion, its shape constantly shifting and composed of various stars and galaxies.⁠

Whiterock

Whiterock is a town located on the bank of the Yolubilis River, 50 miles south of Kintargo. It has long been maintained by the wealthy House Jhaltero, and originated as a stop where rocks mined from Jhaltero quarries were smoothed and catalogued for shipment to Kintargo, but has since grown into a market town for local farmers and ranchers who do not wish to take the long trip to the capital. Its ruler, Canton Jhaltero, is casual and disinterested, viewing himself due an easy life after securing his family's place on the Silver Council.⁠
1803467481:
Selkelas

An enormous headless stone torso known as Selkelas is half-buried near the western edge of the Katapesh desert. Its size indicates that, had it been a fully detailed humanoid statue, it would have measured at least 20 feet in height. The name "Selkelas" is engraved on the statue's back. One of its granite hands seems to have been carved to hold a now-missing weapon, perhaps a sword.⁠
1803561531:
Ñarula

Ñarula is a city in the south-west of Xopatl that once thrived on logging the nearby Manzinago Forest, but has been forced to adapt to the ever-growing danger of the Deepweave infestation.⁠

Ñarula once grew rich from exporting timber across Xopatl and to the neighbouring kingdom of Nalmeras, but the forest has since grown dangerous from the Deepweave infestation of carnivorous plants that devour any who enter it. The people of Ñarula have taken to ranching by using arcane secrets shared by the city of Jolizpan. Ñarula's citizens have created their own arcane ley lines near their ranches which has resulted in huge livestock, but some locals fear that because of their prodigious size ranchers can no longer control these animals.⁠
1804194671:
Iz

The city of Iz (pronounced IZ)⁠ was the first to fall to the demonic forces which poured out of the Worldwound in 4606 AR.⁠
1824912671:
Duskwarden Guildhouse

The headquarters of the Duskwardens is the Duskwarden Guildhouse: a squat building in the district of Bis marked with a placard of the Duskwardens' Twisted Door badge. Within are a few offices for ranking officials of the group, barracks for new recruits (or any member with no other place to sleep), workshops, and a modest store of equipment.⁠
1831339511:
Wati

Wati, also called the Half-City, is located in southern Osirion at the confluence of the Asp and Crook rivers and the birth of the River Sphinx. It is best-known for its enormous necropolis, or city of the dead, a relic of a bygone plague.⁠⁠
1833776301:
Catacombs

The Catacombs of Absalom are a labyrinthine network of passageways near the Starstone Cathedral where early followers of Aroden are buried. Pilgrims can pass through one of these passages carrying a candle and receiving a coin bearing the image of one of those buried there. In recent decades, the historical value of these coins has skyrocketed, and criminals are selling counterfeit copies to unsuspecting tourists.⁠
1836404791:
Bloom Cabaret

The Bloom Cabaret is a cafe on one of the busiest streets of the district, and behind one of its private rooms lies the entrance to archives used by the Ordaire of Goode Standing, composed of wealthy socialites with a hunger for occult and esoteric knowledge. The Order regularly commissions artists to create art that parodies the Brotherhood of Abadar, and its donations to the Ivy Playhouse give it control over which works are exhibited, when, and who plays which roles. The Order also wields influence over the Ivy District Council because several of its members belong to the organization.⁠
1838631771:
Asmodeus Mirage

The Asmodeus Mirage is (or was, see below) a demiplane created by the destruction of an unnamed herald of Asmodeus by Rovagug. A connection between it and Golarion appears once every 100 years in the deserts of northwestern Katapesh, hard against the Brazen Peaks and north-northwest of the source of the Pale River. This connection remains open for a single 24-hour period before disappearing again for a century.⁠⁠
1845727951:
Forestheart

Forestheart is a powerful rift between Golarion and the First World. It is a dark glade in the ancient Grungir Forest surrounded by giant trees. In the center of the glade there is an otherworldly calm and clear pool. By observing the reflections in the water's surface a visitor could look at any place in the First World and, by leaping into the pool, he could be transported to the place the pool was reflecting. The journey is one-way and the visitor has to find another way back. A capricious and demanding nymph named Imavajana guards the pool and controls the destinations.⁠
1847037241:
Braganza

Braganza is a city on the Plains of Molthune on the western edge of that country, and is one of the centers of the worship of Abadar in the region.⁠
1867954151:
Rakarit

Rakarit is the capital of Valash Raj, a city built using construction techniques copied from the ruins of past empires. Kaiju callers and weather masters protect the city from disasters. The palace appears to be made from a single block of stone, and hundreds of minarets and towers rise above the treetops. The ruins of the Valashai empire are used to heat the city through generators, creating residential districts in pods where thousands of workers slept. Kaiju callers use discs to orally transmit their knowledge. The capital is the intellectual center of the nation, housing magic schools that seek to uncover the secrets of the ruins, and many of their graduates become adventurers to bring these treasures back.⁠
1901657281:
Riverspire

The elven town of Riverspire is located on the Kyonin River in the southwest of the country. It grew from a single family, and the majority of its inhabitants today are still distantly related to one another.⁠
1906735631:
Quldari's Vault

Quldari's Vault is an enormous vault buried deep in the depths of the grasslands of Xopatl. Quldari's Vault was created by Quldari, a beastkin who was one of the last remaining hero-gods of Xopatl's ancient history. Seeing that this era of the hero-gods was finally coming to an end, Quldari created an enormous solid obsidian vault that he said contained everything Xopatl would need to survive in the future. The mages of Xopatl were finally able to open the first door in -2311 AR but, to their surprise, found nothing of value in the first chamber. Since then, in total, thirty three doors have been opened and, so far, no treasure has ever been found, only more obstacles and doors.⁠
1908178671:
Cave of a Thousand Stars

The Cave of a Thousand Stars is a system of caves created by a moot of muldnal agathions in an area of Vudra where the planar boundaries between the Universe and Nirvana grow thin. It is a place where the otherworldly perfection of Nirvana seeps into Golarion as a palpable presence and, as such, is sought out by monks and scholars alike.⁠
1908998561:
Oroskirr

Oroskirr, also known as the Opal Island or the Ever-Watching Eye, is a strange opalescent dome that rises from the waters of the Nyvyrd in northern Iobaria. The dome glows and crackles with energy every night, and draws lightning to its surface during thunderstorms. Its surface has never been breached, but locals presume it is the source of the Nyvyrd's unusually warm waters.⁠
1933732871:
Seidoyaji

Seidoyaji (pronounced say-doh-yah-jee)⁠ is one of the many cities that dot the tengu kingdom of Kwanlai. The thieves' guild of Seidoyaji is responsible for the Autumn of Iron Tears, a conflict with the thieves' guild of the city of Todorokaze that escalated into a full-blown proxy war between the two cities.⁠
1934680311:
Wyvernsting

Wyvernsting, formerly called Wyvern's Sting,⁠ is the second largest settlement in Belkzen by population. It is located in the north-easternmost spur of the Kodar Mountains, surrounded by a high wooden stockade. It controls one of the Belkzen's rare forests and is close to the valuable and dangerous beasts of the Realm of the Mammoth Lords to the north, bringing wealth and power to its rulers.⁠

As of 4724 AR, Unbroken Horn Hold chief Paskis Nine-Knives rules Wyvernsting. She succeeded her predecessor Hundux Half-Man around 4716 AR after overthrowing and executing him in a three-day-long coup.⁠
1937985461:
Wisdom's Refuge

Wisdom's Refuge is where the district's Wise Council conducts its administrative activities, focusing on education and the arts. To further their goals, many institutions dedicated to preserving history or knowledge receive reduced taxes, which are then passed on to students at the district's numerous schools and academies. Many council members have studied at the Arcanamirium, so they are aware of the dangers of magic manipulating elections and ensure that all processes adhere to the district's philosophy of fairness.⁠
1938743271:
Guardians

The Guardians are a monument in Magnimar's Naos district, located just inside the Twins' Gate at the south end of the Avenue of Hours.⁠ Two 200-foot-tall statues depict the local twin heroes Cailyn and Romre Vanderale, who saved the burgeoning settlement of Magnimar from a shriezyx attack unleashed from the Irespan. The statues wield flaming staves that form the namesake arch of the city's Grand Arch district. Scholars of magic maintain that studying this monument improved their concentration.⁠⁠

Shaping Bluffs

The Shaping Bluffs are a two-mile-long geological feature along the Sellen River and the border it forms with Galt, and is known for the mysterious tendency of its bluffs to constantly reshape their faces. The steep cliffs expose red stone that changes erratically regardless of any winds or waters and can hide or reveal caves at water level.⁠

The cliffs house a camp of dwarven stone shamans and geomancers, led by Hromcul Stetruk, who have stabilized their location enough to continue studying the phenomenon. The Shaping Bluffs are also used by river pirates who take advantage of the transient nature of caves that appear and disappear along the water level to raid traffic along the Sellen River.⁠
1966443981:
High Isle

High Isle, along with its sister city of Low Isle, provides much of the seafood for the nation of Xopatl. Located along the south-western coast of Xopatl on a small island in Lake Tapipallati, High Isle is renowned for its seafood. The fishermen of High Isle go on weeks-long fishing trips into the lake's depths to hunt for giant catfish and other large lake monsters.⁠⁠
1975540211:
Stinger's Scar

Stinger's Scar was a park called Celestial Pleasure Ground where the elite could spend their time enjoying its verdant gardens, but when an earthquake struck the city, a vermin infestation appeared out of nowhere. From wasps to flies to worms, all kinds of insects began consuming the vegetation, and for some inexplicable reason, new species of these vermin kept appearing. The place is avoided by the neighborhood, which doesn't know why the insects are staying in the park or why they were attracted there, and researchers have observed humanoid shapes in the swarms of flies dancing without any human features on their faces.⁠ The central creature of these stories has been presented as the Scorpion Prince, and its nature is not just a story to tell children at night.⁠
1984375031:
District Courthouse

The District Courthouse in the Precipice Quarter, like many parts of the district, was abandoned following the earthquake that shook the city. The judges sealed the building with barricades after wrongfully executing Jarbin Mord, and his spirit is said to haunt the white marble halls of this crumbling four-story building.⁠
1991038651:
Aevolar's Crossing

Aevolar's Crossing looks like a safe crossing of the Usk River, but this is wrong. A Chelaxian army once tried and failed to cross here, and their bones and rusted armor remain as a reminder.⁠
2000915951:
Broken Hook

Broken Hook is the southernmost tip of Taldas Isle in the Shackles, south of the town of Little Oppara. It derives its name from the way the craggy land breaks off into countless small rocks and islets and trails off into the sea. The children of Little Oppara play here, daring each other to see who can hop farthest away from land while jumping from boulder to boulder. They also claim that the Broken Hook is home to an oceanic giant, but as of 4712 AR, this had been dismissed as a fairy tale until a spate of recent disappearances.⁠
2001464931:
Cesca

Cesca is a settlement in eastern Ustalav, located in the county of Varno.⁠⁠
2001960891:
Ogrekin Hall

Ogrekin is a transporting business located in the Docks district of Absalom. Ogrekin can move anything that needs moving anywhere within the city. Its characteristically strong employees cooperate with the Pilot House and Harbormaster's Grange to get to ships first and offer to move their goods quickly and securely. Its base of operations is a simple building called Ogrekin Hall,⁠⁠ distinguished by two disturbing life-sized ogrekin sculptures that flank its main entrance.⁠

Ogrekin is owned by the Second Harbormaster, Ptarnex Dexarion,⁠⁠ who also owns the city's Red Drake Warehouses.⁠ It is managed by his second-in-command and labormaster Feldreth Noor,⁠⁠ and its employees work with the city's Pilot's House and Harbormaster's Grange.⁠

Thronestep

Thronestep is a port city on the banks of Lake Encarthan, and the capital of the growing theocracy of Razmiran. A city of sharp contrasts, it is among the newest settlements in Avistan, having been built by the Living God's faithful less than 50 years ago.⁠

Wanshi

Wanshi is the capital of Hogosareta Province in Minkai,⁠ as well as the primary commercial port and naval base on the nation's southern coastline.⁠

The Palace of Ivory and Bone is a perverse, desecrated fortress within the holy lands of the Divine Garden region of eastern Vudra.⁠

Belila

Belila is a small Irriseni town of the Iceflow in the northwestern corner of the province of Bleakmarch. Much of the town recently converted to new faith known as the Way of Transcendent Bliss, much to the consternation of its ruler, the Baroness Frederyka.⁠

Swan's Shadow Theater

Swan's Shadow Theater is a venue in the Old Kintargo neighborhood of Kintargo, Ravounel, that fell into ruin during the city's brief rule under Barzillai Thrune in 4715–4716 AR, during which it was confiscated and used by the church of Asmodeus. Following the Kintargan Rebellion its ownership was assumed by the city of Kintargo, and as of 4724 AR it had been abandoned since.⁠

Carrion Hill

The city of Carrion Hill in eastern Ustalav is a strange place, resting atop an unnatural and unsettling mound. Why people choose to live here is unclear, but for some reason they always have.⁠⁠ Varisians first settled Carrion Hill in 2397 AR; prior to this, Carrion Hill was a holy site for the local Kellid tribes.⁠
2057108291:
Erastil's Alehouse

Erastil's Alehouse is a popular establishment run by clergymen of Erastil on the edge of the Avenue of the Hopeful, so there is plenty of traffic to offer courage in the form of beer to those trying to become gods.⁠
2061120531:
Founder's Flame

Founder's Flame is a magical fountain in the Naos district of Magnimar. Antholus Kaddren built it as a gift for city at its founding. Green oil fills the bronze bowl and is perpetually on fire. The color of the fire cycles from yellow to orange to violet to blue. Legend holds that if a spellcaster meditates here, she casts fire-based spells more strongly.⁠
2063132511:
Quantium

Quantium, a port city on the Obari Ocean, is the capital of the nation of Nex. The city prides itself on its diversity; xenophobia is frowned upon. The city has many palaces, hanging gardens, and open-air mazes, as well as several reputable universities of arcane magic and lore. The city's magnificence has been compared with Oppara in Taldor and Sothis in Osirion.⁠

There are many statues of the archmage Nex, who took control of the then-city-state in -987 AR,⁠ as well as of the heroes who helped him forge the kingdom that still bears his name.⁠

Cenotaph

Sitting amidst the hustle and bustle of Bridgeward, the most industrial district of Magnimar's prestigious Summit region, the Cenotaph is a monument to a fallen legend. The Cenotaph is a ten-story-tall, hollow cylindrical monument dedicated to Alcaydian Indros that has become the centre of an impromptu cemetery.⁠

Years after its constructions the friends and family of Alcaydian began to pass away and they requested to be buried either within or around the Cenotaph. These requests soon started to include people who had never known Alcaydian and has now become a true tradition for the cities rich and elite to get buried either beneath the surrounding Mourner's Plaza. Clerics of Pharasma patrol the area, including the catacombs, to protect against undead, scavengers, and grave robbers.⁠⁠

Local legend says that praying in the plaza gives a boost to ones ability to resist physical threats.⁠
